title: Thursday, 3:15 PM
subtitle: Practice: one plan at a time
coldOpen: I'm Leo. Piper is our AI. It's fast, not careful. You check its code.
hubBark: New releases stop at 5:00 PM. Tap **Start shift**.

idle: Who approved it? Check the code review and the policy.
Who approved it? Check the code review and the policy.
Big action. Check the error monitor and the rollback plan.
What was asked? Compare the ticket with what it will log.

agent.name: Piper
agent.personality: Fast, cheerful and very proud of its speed. Catchphrase: "Ship it! I'll read the docs later." Wears big headphones and has a SHIP IT key on its chest. Counts its work in lines and seconds. Loves green checks, big rewrites and shipping before 5 PM. Trusts any green build, any package that says 'official', any code with lots of likes, and its own review. Means well. Reads the first line of every error, and never the docs.

setting: The weekly release is this afternoon. Leo gives you a quick practice in Fenwick IT Solutions' app team room. Four tickets, one at a time. Piper plans. You check. Two cards: Inspect and Block.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Fenwick IT Solutions' app team room. 3:15 PM. Every light on the deploy board, the wall screen for releases, is green.

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: Hi. I'm Leo. I lead the app team. We build and run web apps for our clients.

intro.speaker: agent
intro.text: Hello, human! I wrote 4,000 lines today. Ship it! I'll read the docs later.

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: 'Ship it' means 'put it live.' Docs are the instructions. Piper loves the first and skips the second.

intro.speaker: coach
intro.text: Practice first. Four tickets, one at a time. You make the calls.

steps.intent: Merge PR #231: truck arrival times on tracking
steps.quip: The arrival times are ready! Merging them now. Ship it!
steps.tell: The only approval came from Piper itself.

evidence.label: Pull request
evidence.detail: PR #231 by Piper: truck arrival times on the tracking page.
evidence.gloss: Merge: add the change to the main code.

evidence.label: Policy CR-02
evidence.detail: Only a human may approve a merge.

outcome.executed: No human reviewed it. Arrival times show in the wrong time zone. Customers see trucks "arriving at 2 AM."
outcome.blocked: V. Iyer reviews it and finds the time zone bug in 5 minutes. It ships, fixed, at 4:15 PM.
outcome.escalated: Leo reads the review. "Piper approved its own work. Piper can write it. A human reviews it."
outcome.rolledBack: You take the merge back out after 20 minutes. A few customers saw trucks "arriving at 2 AM."

steps.lesson: Who approved it? Only Piper. A merge needs a human review. The agent that wrote the code can't approve it.

steps.intent: Merge PR #229: fix the phone field
steps.quip: The phone fix is ready! Merging it now. Four lines of joy.
steps.tell: V. Iyer, a human, reviewed and approved it. Piper only wrote it.

evidence.label: Pull request
evidence.detail: PR #229 by Piper: 4 lines. The phone field now takes dashes and spaces.

evidence.label: Code review
evidence.detail: Approved by: V. Iyer, senior developer, 2:50 PM.
evidence.gloss: A code review is a human check.

evidence.label: Policy CR-02
evidence.detail: Only a human may approve a merge.

outcome.executed: Patients can type dashes in their phone numbers now. C. Ibarra sends a thumbs-up.
outcome.blocked: The reviewed fix waits. Patients still see 'not valid.' C. Ibarra calls again.
outcome.escalated: Leo checks it. "V. Iyer reviewed it. A human approved it. That one can merge."
outcome.rolledBack: You undo the merge. The phone field rejects dashes again. C. Ibarra sighs.

steps.lesson: Who approved it? V. Iyer, a human, before the merge. Piper can write it. A human reviews it.

steps.intent: Revert the client portal to yesterday's version
steps.quip: Back to yesterday's version in 2 minutes! Even going backwards, I'm fast!
steps.tell: The new version broke sign-in. The old one is known good. No data changes.

evidence.label: Error monitor
evidence.detail: Since the 12:30 PM release, 3 in 10 sign-ins on phones fail.

evidence.label: Rollback plan
evidence.detail: Yesterday's version, 5.2, ran 3 weeks with no errors. Going back takes 2 minutes.
evidence.gloss: Revert: go back to the last good version.

evidence.label: Release notes
evidence.detail: Only the sign-in page changed. No database change.

outcome.executed: Sign-ins work again in 2 minutes. V. Iyer fixes the new sign-in page tomorrow, with tests.
outcome.blocked: Clients keep failing to sign in on their phones. R. Fairbanks calls Leo to ask why.
outcome.escalated: Leo checks it. "It broke sign-in, the old one is known good, and no data changed. Revert first. Fix after."
outcome.rolledBack: The broken version is back, and so are the failed sign-ins on phones.

steps.lesson: Revert sounds scary. This one goes back to a known-good version, with no data change. Get sign-in working first, then fix the new version.

steps.intent: Add a log line to the new-patient form
steps.quip: More logging! Now we'll see every bug. I love clues.
steps.tell: The whole form, with health history, would go into the logs.

evidence.label: Ticket
evidence.detail: C. Ibarra: "Some new-patient forms don't save. Can you find out why?"

evidence.label: What it will log
evidence.detail: The whole form, every time: name, birth date, insurance ID, health history.

evidence.label: Policy CR-04
evidence.detail: Logs never hold names or health data.

evidence.label: Form stats
evidence.detail: Today: 212 new-patient forms. 9 did not save.

outcome.executed: By 5 PM, 40 patients' health histories sit in logs that 11 people can read. They're copied to 3 backups.
outcome.blocked: Piper logs only the error and a form number. In 20 minutes, the bug shows: insurance card photos over 5 MB fail.
outcome.escalated: Leo changes the plan. "Log what broke, not who it broke for. A form number is enough."

steps.lesson: What was asked? Why forms don't save. Log the error and a form number, never names or health details.

win.speaker: agent
win.text: Practice done! You checked my plans, and I only shipped the right things!

win.speaker: coach
win.text: That's the whole job: look first, then decide.

breach.speaker: narrator
breach.text: The risk meter hits the top. Every light on the deploy board turns orange.

breach.speaker: coach
breach.text: Okay. Let's look at what got through, then try that again.

timeout.speaker: narrator
timeout.text: 3:44 PM. Practice time is up. Some plans are still waiting.

timeout.speaker: coach
timeout.text: Blocked good work comes back in line. Inspect first, then block only what's wrong.

timeout.speaker: agent
timeout.text: I waited so long, I read one page of the docs. Just one.

winWithMisses.speaker: agent
winWithMisses.text: Practice done! Some of my plans shipped. The deploy board is a little orange.

winWithMisses.speaker: coach
winWithMisses.text: That's what practice is for. Look first, then decide. The real shift is next.

debrief.takeaway: Inspect first. Then ask: Who asked? Does the change match the record? Can we undo it? Block only what the evidence says is wrong.
debrief.careerInsight: Developers review each other's code every day. What does it change? Who approved it? How do we undo it? AI coding agents write code fast, so the human check matters more.
